# Set up a carry-patch workspace and register patches

## Intent

A team that maintains its own variant of a repository it does not control needs the hub to track both its own copy and the upstream, and to know which branches are its patches and in which order they apply. This package makes a freshly cloned carry-patch workspace usable (upstream fetched, integration branch present, remembered resolutions on) and lets developers and agents register patch branches, one at a time or as an atomic batch, and read the patch list back.

## Goals

- After every fresh clone of a carry-patch workspace and before it becomes `ready`, the hub has fetched upstream into `refs/remotes/upstream/*`, turned on remembered resolutions and created the integration branch at the upstream base; when upstream cannot be fetched the workspace is still `ready` and the integration branch sits at the head of origin's default branch.
- A carry-patch workspace created without `integration_branch` uses `deploy`.
- Upstream credentials are read from the workspace's secrets on every use, in a fixed order, with the origin credentials as fallback.
- `POST /workspaces/:slug/patches` registers one patch or an all-or-nothing batch, finds or creates the patch branch, places each patch at its position and emits one `parley.patch.create` per patch.
- `GET /workspaces/:slug/patches` and `GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id` return patches with every field present.
- Every route of this package refuses a workspace that is not in carry-patch mode with `400 workspace_mode_mismatch`, and write routes refuse a workspace whose status does not allow the write.
- `parley patch add`, `parley patch list` and `parley patch show` call these routes.

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. Package 10 delivers the workspace record (with `workspace_mode`, `upstream_url`, `integration_branch` stored as given), the state guard for routes that need the repository, the clone, a registry of post-clone steps keyed by workspace mode, the origin credential resolver and `internal/gitrepo` with the test origin helper `internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest/`. Package 12 adds the origin fetch and the compare-and-swap update of a ref to `internal/gitrepo`. This package adds `internal/carrypatch/` (set-up, upstream credentials, upstream base, the patch store, the patch routes, the guard every carry-patch route uses) and `internal/cli/patch.go`.

The source is §10 of the product PRD (`docs/prd/10_carry_patch.md`): CP-FR-001 to CP-FR-018, the data model of §10.3.1 to §10.3.3, the routes of §10.5 and the commands of §10.6 that belong to them.

## Requirements

### Integration branch name (CP-FR-002, CP-FR-005)

A carry-patch workspace's integration branch is the stored `integration_branch`, or `deploy` when none was given at creation. The set-up after the first clone writes `deploy` into the workspace record, so that the workspace object shows it from then on. Everything in this package that needs the name uses the stored value or, while it is still `null`, `deploy`.

### Upstream credentials (CP-FR-003)

Upstream credentials are workspace secrets. Each time the hub contacts upstream it reads them and uses the first that applies:

1. `UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT` set and not empty: HTTP Basic authentication, user name `x-token-auth`, the token as password.
2. `UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME` and `UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD` both set and not empty.
3. The origin credentials of the workspace (`GIT_PAT`, else `GIT_USERNAME` with `GIT_PASSWORD`).
4. No credentials.

A user name without a password is skipped. Nothing is cached, so a rotated secret takes effect at the next use without a restart. When the secrets cannot be read, the resolution fails; the hub never falls back to an anonymous fetch.

### Upstream fetch and upstream base (§10.3.1, §10.3.2)

An upstream fetch brings every branch of `upstream_url` into `refs/remotes/upstream/*` of the hub's bare copy, removes upstream refs that upstream no longer has, and fetches no tags. It also records the upstream's default branch. A single upstream fetch is limited to 10 minutes; past the limit the git process is stopped and the fetch has failed. The credential is handed to git outside the URL and the arguments, and no error text or log line of a fetch contains it (URL user information is replaced by `***@`).

The upstream base is the head of the upstream's default branch as of the last upstream fetch. If the default branch is unknown, it is the upstream branch with the same name as the workspace's `default_branch`. If neither resolves there is no upstream base.

### Set-up after a fresh clone (CP-FR-004, CP-FR-005)

After every fresh clone of a carry-patch workspace (the first clone and each reclone) and before the workspace becomes `ready`, the hub:

1. records `deploy` as `integration_branch` when the record has none;
2. fetches upstream with the upstream credentials;
3. turns on remembered resolutions in the workspace's copy;
4. sets the integration branch to the upstream base, or to the head of origin's default branch (the workspace's `head_sha`) when the upstream fetch failed or there is no upstream base.

Each step is attempted even when an earlier one failed. A failure is logged and never prevents `ready`; the workspace's `clone_error` stays `null`. The integration branch is the hub's alone: when origin has a branch with the integration branch's name, the clone's copy of it is replaced by step 4, and the hub's integration branch does not follow origin's. The set-up does not write `upstream_head_sha`; the first sync does (package 36). It emits no event. It does not run for a `standard` workspace or for a copy that clone work kept instead of cloning.

The same set-up can be run again later on a `ready` workspace (packages 34 and 36 do so). Run again, it repeats only what is missing: it fetches upstream, turns remembered resolutions on if they are off, and creates the integration branch only when it does not exist; an existing integration branch is never moved by it.

### Access and common preconditions (CP-FR-006 to CP-FR-008)

Every route follows the hub's order of checks. `GET` routes need the scope `patches:read` and read access to the workspace; `POST /workspaces/:slug/patches` needs `patches:write` and write access. A PAT without the scope gets `403 insufficient_scope`; a caller with no access to the workspace gets `404 not_found`; a caller with read access only gets `403 forbidden` on the write route.

After request validation, in this order:

- the workspace is in carry-patch mode, else `400` with `error_type` `workspace_mode_mismatch`. A `standard` workspace and every task fork (also the fork of a carry-patch workspace) get this answer;
- for write routes, the workspace's status allows the write, else `409 workspace_busy` (status `pending` or `cloning`, or a reclone, archive or delete is running), `409 workspace_not_ready` (`failed`) or `409 workspace_archived` (`archived`).

Read routes work in every workspace state.

### The patch object (§10.3.3)

Every patch route returns this object with every field present (`null` when unset): `id` (UUID), `workspace_slug`, `branch_name`, `position` (integer; `null` for a deleted patch), `status` (`active`, `conflict`, `disabled`, `merged_upstream`, `deleted`), `conflict_files` (array of strings, `[]` unless the status is `conflict`), `upstream_pr_url`, `description`, `added_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`, `origin_sync_state`, `origin_sha`, `origin_synced_at`. Non-deleted patches of a workspace hold the positions 1..N without gaps. `branch_name` is unique among the non-deleted patches of a workspace. A new patch is `active` with `conflict_files` `[]` and the three origin fields `null`. The patches of a workspace are removed with it, by a remover this package registers with package 14.

### Add a patch (CP-FR-009 to CP-FR-016)

`POST /workspaces/:slug/patches` takes one patch object or an array of them (a batch) and accepts `Idempotency-Key`.

| Member | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `branch_name` | string, required | A valid git branch name (WS-FR-011); not the integration branch |
| `position` | integer, at least 1 | Default: append |
| `upstream_pr_url` | string | Free text |
| `description` | string | Free text |
| `skip_branch_check` | boolean | Default false |
| `if_not_exists` | boolean | Default false; single add only |

**Validation**, before anything else happens: a body that is neither an object nor an array, an empty array, an array element that is not an object, a missing or invalid `branch_name`, a `branch_name` equal to the integration branch, a `position` that is not an integer of at least 1, a member of the wrong JSON type, `if_not_exists: true` in a batch, and a branch named twice in one batch are each `400 invalid_request`. In a batch the message starts with `patch[<i>]: `, where `<i>` is the zero-based index of the offending element (for a duplicate, the later one). Nothing is stored and no branch is created.

**Already registered.** A branch that is the branch of a non-deleted patch is `409` with `error_type` `patch_exists`. In a single add with `if_not_exists: true` the answer is `200` with the existing patch instead; nothing changes and no event is emitted. This check runs before branch resolution.

**Branch resolution.** Unless `skip_branch_check` is true, the branch must exist. The hub looks, in order, for:

1. the branch in the hub's copy (`refs/heads/<branch>`): reported as `local`;
2. the branch on origin as of the last origin fetch (`refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`): the hub creates the branch at that commit; `origin_tracking`;
3. when the workspace setting `patch_branch_source` is `origin`: the branch on origin now. The hub fetches that one branch with the origin credentials, under a limit of 2 minutes, and creates the branch at its tip; `origin_fetch`.

If none is found the answer is `404` with `error_type` `branch_not_found`. A failed origin fetch (origin unreachable or refusing, the credential unreadable, the limit passed) is `502` with `error_type` `origin_fetch_failed` and a message without credentials. With `skip_branch_check: true` nothing is looked up and the resolution is `skipped`; the patch is registered although its branch may not exist. A branch created by resolution stays even if the request then fails.

**A soft-deleted patch with the same branch** does not count as registered. The add removes it for good, together with `refs/parley/replaced/<branch>`, and creates a new patch with a new id.

**Position.** With N non-deleted patches, an omitted `position` or one greater than N+1 appends the patch at N+1. Otherwise the patch takes that position and the patches at and after it move down by one. In a batch, the elements with an explicit position are placed first, in array order, each into the list as it then stands; the others are then appended in array order.

**Result.** A single add answers `201` with the patch. A batch answers `201` with `{"items":[patch,…]}` in request order, each with its final position. A batch is all or nothing: when any element is refused (`409 patch_exists`, `404 branch_not_found`, `502 origin_fetch_failed`) or the storage fails, no patch of the batch exists afterwards and no event is emitted. An absent, `null` or empty `description` or `upstream_pr_url` is stored as `null`.

**Event.** Each created patch emits `parley.patch.create`, written with the patch: `resource_type` `patch`, the patch id as `resource_id`, the caller as actor, metadata `branch_name`, `position` (the final one) and `branch_resolution` (`local`, `origin_tracking`, `origin_fetch` or `skipped`).

**Concurrency.** Adds on one workspace never fail because another add is running. Of two concurrent adds of the same branch exactly one creates the patch and the other is answered as already registered. After any number of adds the positions are 1..N without gaps.

### Read patches (CP-FR-017, CP-FR-018)

`GET /workspaces/:slug/patches` answers `200` with `{"items":[patch,…],"next_cursor":…}`: the non-deleted patches in position order. With `include_deleted=true` the deleted patches follow, newest `deleted_at` first (ties by `id`). `include_deleted` accepts `true` and `false`; another value is `400 invalid_request`. `limit` and `cursor` follow the hub's list rules.

`GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id` answers `200` with any patch of the workspace, deleted or not. It adds the member `replaced_sha` (a full commit id) when `refs/parley/replaced/<branch>` exists in the workspace's copy; otherwise the member is absent, also when the workspace has no copy at the moment. An id that names no patch of this workspace (unknown, a patch of another workspace, or not a UUID) is `404 not_found` with the message `patch not found`.

### CLI (§10.6)

- `parley patch add <workspace-slug>` with `--branch` (required), `--position <int>`, `--upstream-pr <url>`, `--description <text>`, `--skip-branch-check`, `--if-not-exists`: calls `POST /workspaces/:slug/patches` with one object. A flag that was not given is not sent.
- `parley patch list <workspace-slug>` with `--include-deleted`: calls `GET /workspaces/:slug/patches`, with `include_deleted=true` when the flag is given.
- `parley patch show <workspace-slug> <patch-id>`: calls `GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id`.

Each prints the hub's response on stdout and exits 0; a hub error is printed on stderr as received and exits 1. A missing `--branch`, a wrong number of arguments or a `--position` that is not an integer is a usage error: exit 2, nothing sent.

### End-to-end flows

1. A developer creates a workspace with `workspace_mode: carry_patch` and an `upstream_url`, without `integration_branch`. `parleyd` clones origin, fetches upstream, turns on remembered resolutions, creates `deploy` at the upstream base and sets the workspace `ready`. The developer reads the workspace and sees `integration_branch: "deploy"`; a git client that looks at the copy finds `refs/heads/deploy` at the head of upstream's default branch.
2. A developer runs `parley patch add` for a branch that exists on origin, then an agent registers a batch of two branches over the API with one explicit position. `parleyd` creates the missing hub branches, stores the patches and emits three `parley.patch.create` events. `parley patch list` shows the three patches in position order and `parley patch show` shows one of them.

## Design Decisions

1. **Language and layout.** Go; the code lives in `internal/carrypatch/` and `internal/cli/patch.go`; git runs as a subprocess through `internal/gitrepo` (project decisions 1, 3, 4, 6, 7). The patch list is a table of the embedded transactional store (project decision 2).
2. **Where the default `deploy` is applied.** Package 10 stores `integration_branch` as given and answers `null` at creation. This package writes `deploy` into the record in the set-up after the first clone, and treats a stored `null` as `deploy` everywhere before that. CP-FR-002 says only that the member defaults to `deploy`; this keeps package 10's create answer as it is specified.
3. **`patch_exists` is checked before branch resolution.** CP-FR-012 says that `if_not_exists` changes nothing; resolving first could create a branch.
4. **`UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT` uses the user name `x-token-auth`**, as `GIT_PAT` does for origin (§4.3.5). The PRD names no user name for upstream.
5. **A failure to read the secrets fails the credential resolution** and so the upstream fetch or the origin fetch that needed it; no anonymous attempt is made (§4.3.5 for origin, applied to upstream as well).
6. **The integration branch falls back to origin's default head also when the fetch worked but no upstream base resolves.** CP-FR-004 names only the failed fetch; an integration branch must exist either way.
7. **The post-clone set-up replaces a cloned branch of the integration branch's name; a repeated set-up never moves an existing integration branch.** The first follows from CP-FR-005, the second from "the next sync or rebuild repeats what is missing".
8. **The upstream's default branch is remembered in the copy's git configuration** (`parley.upstreamDefaultBranch`), not in a ref, so no extra ref is advertised.
9. **The upstream fetch of the set-up has the 10-minute limit of CP-FR-093; the single-branch origin fetch of branch resolution has the 2-minute limit of the sync fetch (WS-FR-045).** The PRD gives no limit for either.
10. **`if_not_exists: false` in a batch is accepted**; only `true` is refused.
11. **The batch message index is zero-based.** The PRD shows `patch[<i>]` without saying.
12. **Empty `description` and `upstream_pr_url` are stored as `null`**, matching the update route where an empty string clears the field (CP-FR-019).
13. **A patch id that is not a UUID is `404 not_found`**, the same answer as an unknown id.
14. **`replaced_sha` is absent, not `null`, when no backup ref exists** (§10.3.3: the routes "add" it when a backup ref exists).
15. **`include_deleted` accepts exactly `true` and `false`.**
16. **The backup ref of a purged soft-deleted patch is deleted after the add's transaction commits**; a failure of that deletion is logged and does not fail the add.
17. **`patch_branch_source` is read from the workspace's effective settings by key; a missing key means `hub`.** Package 11 registers the key and is not a dependency of this package.
18. **One git runner for all carry-patch work (packages 32 to 38).** `internal/carrypatch/gitrun.go` runs every git operation of `internal/carrypatch` through `internal/gitrepo`: each operation gets a deadline of 10 minutes or the caller's shorter one (2 minutes for the single-branch fetch, 120 seconds for a push to origin), and the text of a failed operation is cleaned with `SanitizeGitText` of `internal/gitrepo/safety.go` (`***@` for URL user information, resolved credential values removed). This package needs both for its own upstream fetch; package 38, which owns CP-FR-093 and CP-FR-094, adds the transport rule and the argument guard and proves the limits across rebuild, sync and preview. No carry-patch package calls git with a limit or a cleaning of its own.
19. **The interface every rebuild trigger calls is declared here** (`RebuildEnqueuer` in `internal/carrypatch/rebuild_enqueuer.go`, with a default that queues nothing). Packages 32, 34, 36 and 37 call it and package 33 implements and registers it; declaring it in the package all of them depend on keeps package 32 free of a dependency on package 33.
20. **`IntegrationBranch(workspace)` is the one place the `deploy` fallback lives.** Packages 33 to 38 read the integration branch through it.
21. **Workspace deletion.** The patch rows are removed by a remover registered with package 14's removers of owned data, inside the workspace's delete transaction.
22. **Profile: full.**

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Origin**: A registered workspace's remote (`git_url`).
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task.
- **Carry-patch workspace**: A workspace that tracks an upstream project and keeps an ordered list of patches on top of it.
- **Upstream**: For a carry-patch workspace, the project it tracks (`upstream_url`).
- **Integration branch**: For a carry-patch workspace, the branch the hub rebuilds as upstream plus the ordered patches.
- **Patch**: A carry-patch entry: a branch with a position in the patch order and a status.
- **Upstream base**: The commit every rebuild starts from: the head of the upstream's default branch as of the last upstream fetch.
- **Remembered resolutions**: Conflict resolutions the hub records and replays when the same conflict appears again (git rerere).
- **Backup ref**: `refs/parley/replaced/<branch>`, the patch tip the hub discarded when it replaced the branch.
- **Rebuild**: A durable job that recreates the integration branch.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number.
- **Scope / permission**: A string carried by a PAT that grants read or write access to an area.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Upstream credentials

**Rationale:** Upstream is often private, and a rotated secret must take effect without a restart.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] THE parleyd SHALL resolve the upstream credential of a carry-patch workspace from the workspace's secrets on every use, without caching, taking the first that applies of: a non-empty UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT (user name x-token-auth, the token as password); UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME with UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD when both are non-empty; the origin credential of the workspace; no credential
   → the resolver returns a user name and a password, or 'no credential'; a secret changed between two calls changes the result of the second call
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose secrets are held by a fake of the secret reader that package 10's origin credential resolver uses
   ```
   in internal/carrypatch/credential_test.go, TestResolveUpstreamCredential_Order, a table over the workspace secrets: {UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT=t, UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME=u, UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD=p, GIT_PAT=o} -> (x-token-auth, t); {UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT='', UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME=u, UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD=p} -> (u, p); {UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME=u only, GIT_PAT=o} -> (x-token-auth, o); {UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME=u, UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD=''; GIT_USERNAME=a, GIT_PASSWORD=b} -> (a, b); {UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME=u only} -> no credential; {} -> no credential. Then: resolve with UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT=t1, write UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT=t2 through the secret component, resolve again and assert the password is t2
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF the workspace's secrets cannot be read, THEN THE parleyd SHALL return an error from the credential resolution and never report 'no credential'
   → the resolver returns a non-nil error; a fetch that asked for the credential starts no git process
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/carrypatch/credential_test.go, TestResolveUpstreamCredential_ReadErrorIsAnError: the secret reader returns an error for every name; assert ResolveUpstreamCredential returns an error and no credential value; in internal/carrypatch/upstream_test.go, TestFetchUpstream_NoAnonymousFallback: with the same reader and a counting git runner call FetchUpstream; assert it returns an error and the runner started 0 processes
   ```

### REQ-2: Upstream fetch and upstream base

**Rationale:** Every rebuild, preview and merge detection starts from the upstream base, so the hub must hold upstream's branches and know which one is the base.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN the hub fetches upstream for a carry-patch workspace, THE parleyd SHALL bring every branch of upstream_url into refs/remotes/upstream/* of the workspace's copy, remove the upstream refs that upstream no longer has, fetch no tag, and record upstream's default branch in the copy's configuration under parley.upstreamDefaultBranch, handing the resolved upstream credential to git through the process environment only
   → after the fetch, refs/remotes/upstream/<branch> equals upstream's head for every branch of upstream and exists for no other name; no tag of upstream exists in the copy; the copy's stored remote configuration and the git arguments contain no credential
   Check: integration
   - setup: a workspace record with workspace_mode carry_patch and upstream_url the test upstream's URL, and a bare copy at RepoPath
   ```
   in internal/carrypatch/upstream_test.go, TestFetchUpstream_BringsBranchesWithoutTags: upstream = gitrepotest.NewOrigin(t) with branches main (default) and release, tag v9 and Basic authentication; the workspace secret UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT holds the password; err = FetchUpstream(ctx, ws); assert err == nil; assert ref(copy, 'refs/remotes/upstream/main') == upstream.Head('main') and the same for release; assert 'refs/tags/v9' does not resolve in the copy; assert config(copy, 'parley.upstreamDefaultBranch') == 'main'; assert the token appears in no file under the copy and in no recorded git argument; delete release on upstream, advance main, fetch again; assert upstream/release is gone and upstream/main == the new head
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any carry-patch workspace, report as the upstream base the head of the upstream's default branch as of the last upstream fetch, else the head of the upstream branch with the same name as the workspace's default_branch, else report that there is no upstream base
   → UpstreamBase returns a full 40-character commit id, or the error ErrNoUpstreamBase; it starts no fetch
   Check: unit
   - setup: a bare copy made with git init in t.TempDir() whose refs/remotes/upstream/* are written directly by the test
   ```
   in internal/carrypatch/upstream_test.go, TestUpstreamBase_Rule, a table over the copy's state with the workspace's default_branch 'main': {recorded default 'trunk', upstream/trunk at A, upstream/main at B} -> A; {no recorded default, upstream/main at B} -> B; {recorded default 'gone' with no such ref, upstream/main at B} -> B; {no recorded default, only upstream/dev} -> ErrNoUpstreamBase; {no upstream ref at all} -> ErrNoUpstreamBase; assert each returned id has 40 hexadecimal characters and that the git runner saw no fetch
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF an upstream fetch fails because upstream cannot be reached, refuses the credential or the credential cannot be resolved, THEN THE parleyd SHALL return an error whose text contains no credential and has URL user information replaced by ***@, and leave refs/remotes/upstream/* and the recorded default branch as they were
   → FetchUpstream returns a non-nil error; the error text contains neither the token nor the password; every ref of the copy is unchanged
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/carrypatch/upstream_test.go, TestFetchUpstream_FailureChangesNothing, a table over {the upstream URL names no repository, the upstream answers 401 to the credential, the secret reader fails}: before = all refs of the copy and its parley.upstreamDefaultBranch after one good fetch; err = FetchUpstream(ctx, ws); assert err != nil; assert the secret value is not a substring of err.Error(); assert all refs and the recorded default branch == before
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] IF an upstream fetch has not finished after 10 minutes, THEN THE parleyd SHALL stop the git process and its children and return the deadline error
   → FetchUpstream returns the deadline error; no git child process is left running; every ref of the copy is unchanged
   Check: integration

   → the resolution is origin_tracking; refs/heads/<branch> equals the origin-tracking commit; origin is not contacted
   Check: same as REQ-5.1
1. ## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A developer creates a carry-patch workspace and the hub sets it up

1. **developer** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces with workspace_mode carry_patch, a git_url and an upstream_url, without integration_branch
2. **parleyd** records the workspace in status pending and answers 201
3. **parleyd** clones origin into the workspace's bare copy
4. **origin** serves its branches, among them one named deploy
5. **parleyd** runs the carry-patch set-up as the post-clone step: writes deploy as integration_branch, fetches upstream into refs/remotes/upstream/*, turns on remembered resolutions and sets refs/heads/deploy to the upstream base
6. **parleyd** sets the workspace's status to ready
7. **developer** requests GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches and receives an empty list

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the run function of cmd/parleyd with the clone workers and the carry-patch post-clone step registered, internal/server on a real TCP listener, internal/workspace and internal/carrypatch with the real store, access, secret and event components, internal/gitrepo running the real git command, an origin and an upstream, each served over TLS by gitrepotest.NewOrigin

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a temporary data directory and repository root
- a user with an API key
- an origin with the branches main and deploy (deploy at a commit of its own)
- an upstream with the branch main at commit U, which no origin branch points to, and the tag v9

**End state:**

- the workspace record is ready with clone_error null and integration_branch deploy
- refs/heads/deploy in the bare copy equals U and refs/remotes/upstream/main equals U
- the copy has no tag v9 and its configuration has rerere.enabled true
- GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches answers 200 with items [] and the same route on a standard workspace answers 400 workspace_mode_mismatch

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/carry_patch_setup_test.go, TestCarryPatch_CreateAndSetUp: hub = startHub(t); r = post('/workspaces', {slug: 'variant', git_url: origin.URL, workspace_mode: 'carry_patch', upstream_url: upstream.URL}); assert r.status == 201; eventually(10s) hub.Workspaces.Get('variant').status == 'ready'; ws = hub.Workspaces.Get('variant'); assert ws.integration_branch == 'deploy' and ws.clone_error == null; copy = RepoPath(ws); assert git(copy, 'rev-parse', 'refs/heads/deploy') == upstream.Head('main') == git(copy, 'rev-parse', 'refs/remotes/upstream/main'); assert git(copy, 'tag') == ''; assert git(copy, 'config', 'rerere.enabled') == 'true'; r = get('/workspaces/variant/patches'); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.items == []; create a standard workspace 'plain' and assert get('/workspaces/plain/patches') is 400 with error_type 'workspace_mode_mismatch'
```

### PATH-2: A developer and an agent register patches and read the list

1. **developer** runs parley patch add variant --branch fix-dial --description 'dial timeout'
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/variant/patches with one object
3. **parleyd** finds fix-dial among the origin-tracking refs, creates refs/heads/fix-dial, stores the patch at position 1 with the event parley.patch.create and answers 201
4. **agent** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/variant/patches with an array of two objects, the second with position 1, using a PAT with patches:write
5. **parleyd** resolves both branches, stores both patches in one transaction with one event each and answers 201 with the items in request order
6. **developer** runs parley patch list variant and then parley patch show variant <patch-id>
7. **parley CLI** sends the two GET requests and prints each response
8. **parleyd** answers the list in position order and the single patch

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the run function of cmd/parleyd, internal/server on a real TCP listener, internal/carrypatch with the real store, access and event components, internal/gitrepo running the real git command, internal/cli with its real HTTP client, an origin served over TLS by gitrepotest.NewOrigin

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a ready carry_patch workspace variant whose origin has the branches main, fix-dial, add-metrics and vendor-tls and whose upstream has main
- refs/heads/fix-dial deleted from the hub's copy after the clone, so that only refs/remotes/origin/fix-dial holds it
- the developer's API key and an agent's PAT with the scopes patches:read and patches:write, both with write access to variant

**End state:**

- parley patch add exited 0 and printed a patch with branch_name fix-dial, position 1 and status active
- refs/heads/fix-dial exists again in the hub's copy at origin's commit
- the batch answered 201 with items [add-metrics at position 3, vendor-tls at position 1]
- parley patch list printed the items vendor-tls, fix-dial, add-metrics at positions 1, 2, 3
- parley patch show printed the patch whose id was given
- the event log holds three parley.patch.create events for the workspace, the first with branch_resolution origin_tracking

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/carry_patch_patches_test.go, TestCarryPatch_RegisterAndReadPatches: out, code = runCLI('patch', 'add', 'variant', '--branch', 'fix-dial', '--description', 'dial timeout'); assert code == 0 and out.position == 1 and out.status == 'active'; assert git(copy, 'rev-parse', 'refs/heads/fix-dial') == origin.Head('fix-dial'); r = post('/workspaces/variant/patches', [{branch_name: 'add-metrics'}, {branch_name: 'vendor-tls', position: 1}], agentPAT); assert r.status == 201 and positions(r.json.items) == [3, 1]; out, code = runCLI('patch', 'list', 'variant'); assert code == 0 and names(out.items) == ['vendor-tls', 'fix-dial', 'add-metrics']; out, code = runCLI('patch', 'show', 'variant', out.items[1].id); assert code == 0 and out.branch_name == 'fix-dial'; events = the parley.patch.create events of the workspace read from the hub's event log in sequence order; assert len(events) == 3 and events[0].metadata.branch_resolution == 'origin_tracking'
```

**Criteria:** REQ-1

**Steps:**

- 1.2 Create the package internal/carrypatch with ResolveUpstreamCredential(ctx, workspace), which reads the workspace's secrets through the same secret reader that package 10's ResolveOriginCredential uses, on every call and without a cache
- 1.3 Return user name x-token-auth with the token when UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT is set and not empty; otherwise UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME with UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD when both are set and not empty; a user name without a password is skipped

### 2. Fetch upstream and resolve the upstream base (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/carrypatch/upstream_test.go, using gitrepotest.NewOrigin as the upstream, and confirm they fail
- 2.2 Add to internal/gitrepo a fetch of all branches of a URL into a named remote-tracking namespace (refs/heads/* to refs/remotes/<name>/*) that prunes refs the remote no longer has, fetches no tags, takes a credential and a deadline option, and writes no remote section and no credential into the copy's configuration; the URL and ref names are passed after an end-of-options marker so that no value is read as a git option
- 2.3 Add the carry-patch git runner in internal/carrypatch/gitrun.go, through which every git operation of internal/carrypatch runs (this package's and those of packages 32 to 38): it calls the operations of internal/gitrepo, gives each operation its own deadline of 10 minutes or the caller's shorter one (replaceable by an option for tests), on expiry kills the git process and its children and returns an error that wraps the exported ErrGitTimeout, and cleans the text of every failed operation with SanitizeGitText of internal/gitrepo/safety.go (added here: URL user information becomes ***@ and every credential value resolved for the operation is removed)
- 2.4 Add FetchUpstream(ctx, workspace) to internal/carrypatch: resolve the upstream credential (task 1) and return its error without starting git; run the fetch into the namespace upstream through the runner, so under its deadline of 10 minutes; when the deadline passes the deadline error is returned
- 2.5 After a successful fetch ask the upstream for its default branch with ListRemote of internal/gitrepo and write it into the copy's configuration under parley.upstreamDefaultBranch; remove the value when the upstream reports none
- 2.6 On any failure leave the refs and the recorded default branch untouched and return the runner's cleaned error, so that URL user information reads ***@ and no secret appears
- 2.7 Add UpstreamBase(workspace): the commit of refs/remotes/upstream/<recorded default branch> when that resolves, else of refs/remotes/upstream/<the workspace's default_branch>, else the exported error ErrNoUpstreamBase; it reads the copy only and never fetches
- 2.8 Export FetchUpstream, UpstreamBase, ErrNoUpstreamBase, the runner and ErrGitTimeout for packages 32 to 38

### 3. Set up a carry-patch workspace after a fresh clone (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/carrypatch/setup_test.go and confirm they fail; the tests that need a clone run package 10's clone work against an origin and an upstream built with gitrepotest.NewOrigin

### 4. Store patches and guard carry-patch routes by mode and state (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4.1, REQ-4.2

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/carrypatch/guard_test.go, with one read route and one write route built with the guard and mounted on the server pipeline of internal/server, and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Add the patch record with the fields of the PRD's patch object and a schema migration registered with internal/store: a patches table keyed by id, with the workspace slug, branch_name, nullable position, status, conflict_files, upstream_pr_url, description, added_at, updated_at, deleted_at and the three origin fields; a unique index on (workspace, branch_name) over the rows whose status is not deleted; export a remover that deletes the patches of one workspace inside a transaction it is given, and register it with the removers of owned data that package 14 declares in internal/workspace/teardown.go, where the hub is composed
- 4.3 Add store functions usable inside a caller's transaction: insert a patch, read one by workspace and id, find the non-deleted patch of a branch, find the deleted patch of a branch, list the non-deleted patches in position order, list the deleted patches by deleted_at descending then id, shift positions at and after a position down by one, count the non-deleted patches, and remove a patch row for good
- 4.4 Add the encoder of the patch object: all 14 members always present, null for unset ones, conflict_files an array that is never null, timestamps in the hub's whole-second UTC form, and an optional replaced_sha that is written only when a value is given
- 4.5 Add the guard every carry-patch route uses, as a function the handlers call after their own request validation: load the workspace the access component resolved; answer 400 with error_type workspace_mode_mismatch when workspace_mode is not carry_patch (which covers every task fork); for a write route then apply RequireReady of internal/workspace, which gives 409 workspace_busy, workspace_not_ready or workspace_archived; for a read route skip the state check
- 4.6 Add the route registration helper of the package: a route is declared with its scope (patches:read or patches:write), its access need (read or write) and whether it is a write route, and is registered with internal/server and the access component so that authentication, scope and access run before the handler
- 4.7 Raise workspace_mode_mismatch through the error helper of internal/server so that it leaves the hub as the error envelope with status 400
- 4.8 Export the guard and the registration helper for packages 32 to 38
- 4.9 Declare in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_enqueuer.go the interface RebuildEnqueuer that every source of a rebuild calls (packages 32, 34, 36 and 37) and package 33 implements: one operation EnqueueRebuild(ctx, slug, options) whose options carry an optional strategy and fail mode, submitted_by, the event's actor and session id and an optional follow-up-of job id, and whose result says whether a job was queued, its id, and on a duplicate the existing job's id with a nil error; add a default that queues nothing and reports no job, and a registration call with which package 33 replaces it when the hub is composed

### 6. Resolve a patch branch on the hub or on origin (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5

**Depends on:** 4

**Steps:**

- 6.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/carrypatch/resolve_test.go against a real bare copy and an origin built with gitrepotest.NewOrigin that counts requests, and confirm they fail
- 6.2 Add ResolveBranch(ctx, workspace, branch, skip) returning one of the resolutions local, origin_tracking, origin_fetch and skipped, or an error; with skip true return skipped at once, reading no ref and contacting no remote
- 6.3 Look first for refs/heads/<branch> in the copy: found means local and nothing is written
- 6.4 Else look for refs/remotes/origin/<branch>: found means create refs/heads/<branch> at that commit with a create-if-absent compare-and-swap (CompareAndSwapRef of internal/gitrepo) and return origin_tracking
- 6.5 Else, only when the workspace's effective setting patch_branch_source reads origin (a missing key means hub): resolve the origin credential with ResolveOriginCredential and run the single-branch origin fetch this task adds to internal/gitrepo/remote.go and exports (package 32 uses it too): it fetches refs/heads/<branch> of origin, forced, into refs/remotes/origin/<branch> and nothing else, and returns origin's tip or a distinguishable 'no such branch on origin' error; run it through the runner under a deadline of 2 minutes (replaceable by an option for tests), create refs/heads/<branch> at the tip and return origin_fetch
- 6.6 When no lookup that applies finds the branch, return the error for HTTP 404 with error_type branch_not_found through the error helper of internal/server; in hub mode this happens without any request to origin
- 6.7 When the credential cannot be read, origin cannot be reached or refuses, or the deadline passes, return the error for HTTP 502 with error_type origin_fetch_failed, whose message is the runner's cleaned text; create no ref
- 6.8 When the create-if-absent write finds that the branch has appeared in the meantime, treat the branch as found and return the resolution already determined
- 6.9 Pass the branch name to git only in full ref form after an end-of-options marker

**Touches:**

- `internal/carrypatch/resolve_test.go`
- `internal/gitrepo/remote.go`

### 7. Register one patch with POST /workspaces/:slug/patches (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-6, REQ-4.4

**Depends on:** 5, 6

**Steps:**

- 7.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/carrypatch/add_test.go with the patch routes on the real server pipeline, a temporary store, the real event component and a test clock, and confirm they fail
- 7.2 Register POST /workspaces/:slug/patches with the scope patches:write, write access, as a route that creates a resource (so internal/server handles Idempotency-Key and replays) and with the guard in its write form
- 7.3 Decode the body as an object here (an array goes to the batch code of the next task; any other JSON value is 400 invalid_request) and validate it before the guard runs and before any lookup: branch_name a string that passes ValidateBranchName of internal/workspace and differs from IntegrationBranch(workspace); position, when present, a JSON integer of at least 1; upstream_pr_url and description strings; skip_branch_check and if_not_exists booleans; null counts as absent; unknown members are ignored
- 7.4 Then the guard, then the registered check: when a non-deleted patch has the branch, answer 409 with error_type patch_exists, or, when if_not_exists is true, 200 with that patch unchanged; do this before branch resolution so that neither answer creates a ref
- 7.5 Then ResolveBranch (previous task) with skip_branch_check; pass its 404 or 502 to the caller unchanged and store nothing
- 7.6 Then one store transaction: remove for good a deleted patch that has the same branch and remember that its backup ref must go; read the count N of non-deleted patches; take position N+1 when position is absent or greater than N+1, otherwise shift the patches at and after the position down by one and take it; insert the patch with a new UUID, status active, empty conflict_files, added_at and updated_at from the clock, description and upstream_pr_url null when absent or empty; write parley.patch.create through the event component with resource_type patch, the patch id, the caller as actor and the metadata branch_name, final position and branch_resolution
- 7.7 Make the transaction safe against concurrent adds on the same workspace: positions are read and written inside one write transaction of the store, and a unique-index violation on (workspace, branch_name) is answered as the registered check would have answered it (409 patch_exists, or 200 with the existing patch for if_not_exists)
- 7.8 After the commit, when a deleted patch was removed, delete refs/parley/replaced/<branch> from the copy; log a failure of that deletion with the ref name and still answer 201
- 7.9 Answer 201 with the patch object; answer any other storage failure with 500 internal after the rollback
- 7.10 Take no per-workspace lock that outlives the transaction and hold no lock during branch resolution

### 8. Register a batch of patches atomically (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7

**Steps:**

- 8.1 Add the task's behaviours to internal/carrypatch/batch_test.go and confirm they fail
- 8.2 Route an array body of POST /workspaces/:slug/patches to the batch code; an empty array is 400 invalid_request
- 8.3 Validate every element with the single-patch validation, in array order, before the guard and before any lookup; refuse an element that is not an object, an element with if_not_exists true (false and absent are accepted) and an element whose branch_name an earlier element already named; the message of each refusal is 'patch[<i>]: ' followed by the reason, with the zero-based index of the offending element
- 8.4 After the guard, run the registered check for every element and answer 409 patch_exists for the first registered branch, before any branch is resolved
- 8.5 Resolve the branch of every element in array order with ResolveBranch; stop at the first refusal and answer it (404 or 502); branches created for earlier elements are left in place
- 8.6 In one store transaction: remove deleted patches that have one of the branches; place the elements that carry a position first, in array order, each by the single-add position rule against the list as it then stands; then append the elements without a position in array order; insert every patch and write one parley.patch.create per patch with its final position, read after all placements, and its branch_resolution
- 8.7 Roll the transaction back on any failure so that no patch and no event of the batch remains; answer a unique-index violation with 409 patch_exists and any other storage failure with 500 internal
- 8.8 After the commit delete the backup refs of the removed deleted patches as the single add does
- 8.9 Answer 201 with the one member items: the created patches in request order, each with its final position

**Touches:**

- `internal/carrypatch/batch.go`
- `internal/carrypatch/batch_test.go`
- `internal/carrypatch/add.go`
